text: [3:421] No accidental “occurrence”: Because termination of employment is an intentional act, all claims arising out of such termination are subject to the same coverage analysis discussed above (¶ 3:357); i.e., since the termination is not an accidental “occurrence,” there is generally no coverage under a CGL policy. [See Loyola Marymount Univ. v. Hartford Acc. & Indem. Co. (1990) 219 CA3d 1217, 1224-1225, 271 CR 528, 532; American Guarantee & Liab. Ins. Co. v. Vista Med. Supply (ND CA 1988) 699 F.Supp. 787, 790 (applying Calif. law)] • [3:422] If tort claims based on negligence (e.g., negligent infliction of emotional distress, negligent misrepresentation, etc.) are incidental to the termination, there is no coverage.
